scope: Linux x64 ordinary Timestamp.now precision and host-error propagation. Targeted controls, not complete IO or upstream-suite conformance.
findings: Native Lean exposes microseconds while the old Date.now adapter exposed only milliseconds. The private native clock bridge now preserves pinned libc++ conversion and native precision in Node, Deno, and the local rebuilt Bun full runtime.
The C IO wrapper previously ignored clock error envelopes. An injected EIO fails the old-runtime control and reaches ordinary Lean IO.Error.hardwareFault in all three repaired full runtimes.
Released Node, Deno, and Bun pass both precision and error checks for the packaged Wasm32 main. The six existing package IO/main tests passed before the supplementary fixture correction.
Twelve unchanged upstream time, HTTP and file-locking registrations pass with all 7267 original test hashes intact. No results are imported into the separate broad campaign.
retainedDevelopmentAttempts: The first v140 C++ relink failed because its private header copy omitted runtime/object.h; v141 records 135 headers and verifies parent hashes.

The initial package run passed seven of eight tests. The new fault fixture incorrectly expected EIO as otherError; pinned native Lean documents EIO as hardwareFault. Only this supplementary fixture was corrected.

The first full fault-injection harness omitted sibling worker support modules and failed before executing Lean. The corrected private harness supplies those helpers. Both initial failures remain retained.
remainingGaps: Native macOS, Windows and ARM64 clock ABI comparisons remain unexecuted; arithmetic controls do not establish OS conformance.
Full Bun compiler checks use the disclosed local memory64-capacity build and Linux stack helper; packaged checks use released Bun.
The full upstream suites and packaged full-runtime integration remain unfinished. No remaining difference is established fundamental.
